subject.title: fix(exec-approvals): handle same-process sync/async lock contention

question: Is it acceptable for synchronous exec authorization to read the previous committed policy while the same process is writing a newer policy?
rationale: The patch can avoid the availability wedge, but whether stale committed-policy reads are permitted during grants or revocations is a security-boundary decision that tests alone cannot define.

options.title: Require coordinated serialization
options.body: Keep readers ordered with the in-process writer through shared process-local coordination rather than bypassing the lock.

options.title: Accept committed-state reads
options.body: Allow the fallback after documenting the authorization semantics and proving concurrent grant and revocation behavior in a real gateway.

options.title: Reproduce the persistent lock first
options.body: Pause this patch until evidence distinguishes transient contention from an unreleased-lock defect that should be repaired directly.

recommendation.title: Require coordinated serialization
recommendation.body: Keep readers ordered with the in-process writer through shared process-local coordination rather than bypassing the lock.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available routing signal connects this behavior to recent exec-approval race-hardening work in the same module.
